Migrate classic-laddie's local LLM inference OFF Ollama and ONTO llama.cpp (llama-server) + llama-swap, using the first-class nixpkgs NixOS modules (services.llama-swap at nixos/modules/services/networking/llama-swap.nix, services.llama-cpp at nixos/modules/services/misc/llama-cpp.nix). Motivation: Ollama's custom-ggml vendoring broke the nightly rebuild (ollama-cuda 0.32.1 failed to compile, blocking the whole classic-laddie generation); we're moving to the more stable llama.cpp stack. cosmo repo -> normal PR workflow, follow AGENTS.md.

IMPORTANT WORKFLOW CONSTRAINT (a previous attempt failed on this): DO NOT start long-running background jobs (multi-GB model downloads, full CUDA compiles) and then exit/ScheduleWakeup to 'wait' for them — klaus agents are single-shot and will terminate without committing, losing all work. Do ONLY verification that completes synchronously in this session (see VERIFY), then COMMIT and OPEN THE PR before finishing. The heavyweight on-host CUDA build and live model-load test will be done by the coordinator on the host before merge — that is NOT your job.

=== HARD FACTS (already researched — do not re-derive) ===
- Host GPU: single NVIDIA RTX 4090, 24GB VRAM. (docs/classic-laddie-hardware.md is STALE and says 3080 Ti/12GB — ignore it.) allowUnfree already set on this host.
- Current: services.ollama (pkgs.ollama-cuda) in hosts/classic-laddie/default.nix (~line 449-467), listening 127.0.0.1:11434, OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=8192.
- THREE models to preserve, exact underlying model + quant:
    qwen2.5-coder:32b -> Qwen2.5-Coder-32B, Q4_K_M GGUF (~19.9GB)
    qwen3:32b         -> Qwen3-32B, Q4_K_M GGUF (~20.2GB)
    gemma4:26b        -> Gemma 25.8B ('gemma4' family), Q4_K_M GGUF (~18.0GB)
  Keep the llama-swap model IDs IDENTICAL to these strings so open-webui/callers see the same names. For each, pick a reputable public HF GGUF repo (bartowski / unsloth / ggml-org) at Q4_K_M and reference it via llama-server's -hf / --hf-repo flag so llama-server DOWNLOADS THE GGUF AT RUNTIME on first use — you do NOT download anything yourself. For gemma4:26b, identify the right Gemma model and a matching GGUF; if none is cleanly available, use the closest current Gemma ~27B Q4_K_M and note the substitution in the PR.
- VRAM: a 32B Q4_K_M (~20GB) + 8192 KV cache fits ONE MODEL AT A TIME in 24GB. Configure llama-swap to SWAP (load-on-request, unload previous), with an idle TTL so VRAM frees when unused. Do NOT configure concurrent/multiple-resident models. Keep context 8192.

=== ENDPOINT CONTRACT (verified repo-wide) ===
- The ONLY consumer of the local endpoint is services.open-webui (port 8888) in the same file. reel-life uses the Anthropic Claude API, not local inference. Nothing else across ~/hack references 11434/ollama.
- Keep the inference endpoint LOCALHOST-ONLY (127.0.0.1) exactly like ollama — do NOT open it on the firewall. Deliberate security boundary.

=== TASKS ===
1. Remove the services.ollama block.
2. Add services.llama-cpp + services.llama-swap. READ both module option schemas first. Use CUDA-enabled llama.cpp (e.g. pkgs.llama-cpp.override { cudaSupport = true; }). Configure llama-swap with the three models; each model's command runs llama-server with GPU offload (-ngl 99), -c 8192, --hf-repo <repo> (runtime download), bound to localhost. llama-swap should listen on 127.0.0.1:11434 (reuse the port) and serve the OpenAI API (/v1/chat/completions, /v1/models).
3. Persistent model cache: point llama-server's HF cache at a systemd StateDirectory (e.g. /var/lib/llama-swap) so downloaded GGUFs persist across restarts and are NOT in the nix store. Set the relevant env (e.g. HF_HOME / LLAMA_CACHE) in the service.
4. Repoint services.open-webui at the new endpoint: environment = { ENABLE_OLLAMA_API = "False"; OPENAI_API_BASE_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1"; OPENAI_API_KEY = "sk-local"; } (verify exact option names against the current open-webui module).
5. Ensure flake.nix nixpkgs.url is "github:nixos/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable" (NO temporary pin — with ollama-cuda removed the frozen channel builds clean). main currently has no pin; just confirm.
